result.title: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning
result.summary: Large language models perform strongly on standard medical QA but degrade on harder reasoning tasks, where multi-agent debate often fails to beat strong single-model prompting. We argue that a key limitation is that existing systems select experts and retrieve knowledge from the question alone, rather than from gaps that emerge during reasoning. We propose challenge-aware adaptive recruitment: an external CHALLENGER inspects the evolving reasoning trace and identifies specific factual or expertise gaps. These signals trigger targeted knowledge retrieval or mid-discussion specialist recruitment. On the MEDAGENTSBENCH hard subset (862 questions across nine biomedical datasets), upfront retrieval provides little benefit, while challenge-aware in-between retrieval performs better; on a multi-specialist backbone it improves accuracy on 8 of 9 datasets and adds 6 percentage points over Challenger Only. Ablations indicate benefits from both retrieval timing and gap-specific query signals, and a live web-search experiment shows that the timing advantage persists across retrieval backends. For specialist recruitment, self-triggered adaptation is unreliable, whereas Challenger-triggered recruitment raises GPT-4.1-mini MedQA accuracy from 46% to 54%, with positive direction on all tested generalization datasets. Naively combining retrieval and specialist recruitment degrades performance, highlighting the need to coordinate adaptive intervention channels. These results show that when and why external resources are recruited is a key design choice in multi-agent medical reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对医疗多智能体推理在难题上不如强单模型的问题，提出由外部 CHALLENGER 检查演进中的推理轨迹、识别具体事实或专长缺口，据此触发中途知识检索或专家补招；在 MEDAGENTSBENCH 硬子集上比较了检索时机、缺口信号与两种干预通道组合的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 「依据推理轨迹中的缺口决定何时、为何引入外部资源」与 LVR 中动态决定是否重新获取视觉证据、停止或继续思考有结构相似性，而其发现的自触发不可靠、朴素组合检索与专家招募反而掉点，可供核查多通道干预（LOOK 与策略切换）如何协调。
